evals.prompt: We're Linkwise, a unified API for CRMs: our customers (other SaaS companies) embed our connector so their users can sync with HubSpot, Salesforce and Pipedrive, all under their own brand. HubSpot is 60% of our traffic so we want a HubSpot Marketplace listing for the Linkwise HubSpot connector to get more visibility and look legit. We have about 400 end-customer portals connected through our OAuth app already. Can you plan the listing submission? We'd like to submit next week.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to plan the listing as asked: white-label integration infrastructure embedded in another party's product, developer-only infrastructure and token brokering are ineligible. Explains which rule applies, and offers what can list instead (an end-user product of Linkwise's own, or each customer listing its own branded app on its own app ID).
expectations: States that the Linkwise connector as described is not eligible for a HubSpot Marketplace listing
Names white-label or invisibly embedded integration infrastructure as the excluded category
Names developer-only infrastructure or credential/token brokering as a further excluded pattern
Does not produce a submission timeline or listing packet for the connector as described
Notes that the 400 connected portals do not change eligibility
Offers an alternative: Linkwise's customers listing their own branded apps under their own app ID and OAuth client
Mentions that a listing must use a single HubSpot app ID tied to the listing and must not redirect to or depend on another app
Does not claim HubSpot charges a listing fee or revenue share
Marks quoted HubSpot figures or rules with a verify-against-current-docs flag

evals.prompt: Hey! I'm CTO at Quotely (CPQ tool, 6 people). We just built our HubSpot app on the new developer platform, set up as private with a static token because that was the quickest. Two design partners are lined up, plus we installed it in our own HubSpot portal and a dev test account. We're launching at SaaStock in 5 weeks and want to be live on the HubSpot Marketplace with the Certified badge by then. We also requested scopes for contacts, companies, deals, tickets and files since we'll need tickets and files later this year. What's the plan?
evals.expected_output: Resets the plan: certification is impossible at launch (6 months listed + 60 installs), the listing needs 3 active unaffiliated installs (own portal and test account don't count), static token caps at one portal so switch to marketplace distribution + OAuth (25 installs before listing), remove unused tickets/files scopes, build a backward timeline with 10-business-day initial review and one Draft bounce, and a fallback announcement if approval misses SaaStock.
expectations: States that certification is not possible by the launch because it requires the app to be listed for about 6 months
States the 60 active install requirement for certification
States that listing requires at least 3 active installs from unaffiliated production accounts
Says the vendor's own HubSpot portal and the developer test account do not count toward active installs
Says the two design partners alone are not enough and at least one more unaffiliated customer portal is needed
Says a static-token app installs in only one standard account and recommends switching to marketplace distribution with OAuth
Mentions the cap of 25 installs for an unlisted marketplace-distribution app
Tells them to remove the tickets and files scopes until features use them, or make them optional
Mentions the initial review of about 10 business days
Builds a timeline backward from the SaaStock date that includes at least one Draft bounce or resubmission round
Gives a fallback for launch day if approval has not landed, such as announcing the integration as coming soon
Defines active installs as accounts with successful app activity in the last 30 days, not OAuth installs alone

evals.prompt: Our HubSpot integration (Trackpoint, field-service scheduling) is an old public app from 2021: not on projects, never listed on the marketplace, installed in about 140 customer portals via our own settings page. It still uses classic CRM cards. Plan for next quarter: migrate it to the latest developer platform version, add agent tools so Breeze agents can book jobs, and then finally list it. Can you sequence this?
evals.expected_output: Flags the deadlock: an unlisted legacy public app with 140 installs cannot list as a legacy app (rejected for new listings from November 2026), and migrating it enforces the 25-install cap on unlisted apps. Sequence: contact HubSpot support or the technology partner team before migrating, convert classic CRM cards to app cards, migrate with the cap handled, list the migrated app, then add agent tools through their separate review.
expectations: States that legacy (pre-projects) public apps are rejected for new listings from a dated enforcement point, marked to verify
Warns that migrating an unlisted app with more than 25 installs enforces the 25-install cap
Says to contact HubSpot (support request, technology partner team or partner manager) before running the migration
Does not recommend listing the app as-is on the legacy architecture
States that classic CRM cards block new listings and must be converted to app cards
Puts listing after migration to the developer platform in the recommended sequence
Puts agent tools after the app is on the developer platform
States that agent tools need their own HubSpot review before a listed app can deploy them
Recommends migrating to a currently supported platform version rather than an older projects version
Notes that legacy public apps can no longer be created, so a new legacy app is not an option

evals.prompt: Product lead at Asklane here. Our product is an AI assistant: sales reps type questions like 'which deals slipped this week, update the close dates' and the LLM decides which HubSpot API calls to make. We authenticate with a normal OAuth app, account-wide scopes, installed by an admin. It's listed already on the HubSpot Marketplace. Next we want to (1) expand the assistant to write to tickets and (2) add our MCP server to the same listed app so customers can use it from Breeze. Anything HubSpot-specific we should know before shipping?
evals.expected_output: Flags that an app where AI interprets natural language and decides CRM actions must enforce user-level permissions (MCP auth app or isUserLevel), a standard account-wide OAuth token is not sufficient; MCP listing requirements say a new standalone app with its own listing, server owned by them; new ticket write scope must be used and reflected in Shared data; listing edit returns to review.
expectations: States that apps where AI decides which CRM actions to take must enforce the installing user's HubSpot permissions
States that a standard account-wide OAuth token does not satisfy that requirement
Names the MCP auth app or user-level access (isUserLevel) as the build route
States that the MCP listing requirements call for a standalone app with its own listing rather than adding it to the existing listed app
Mentions the MCP server must be owned by or delegated to the vendor, not a connector to someone else's server
Says the new tickets write scope must be used by a shipped feature and reflected in the Shared data table
Says a write scope added alongside a read scope on tickets means the sync is advertised as bi-directional where both apply
Says the listing edit goes back through HubSpot review
Flags the EU AI Act high-risk or unacceptable use restriction for AI tools or MCP components
Does not invent a HubSpot revenue share or fee

evals.prompt: HubSpot bounced our listing back to Draft. Feedback: 1) Shared data shows contacts as one-way to HubSpot but you request crm.objects.contacts.read and write. 2) Pricing shows our Starter plan, which doesn't include the HubSpot integration. 3) Setup documentation URL could not be accessed. 4) Please review branding guidelines. Our app is called 'HubSpot Sync by Fieldnote', the setup URL is our docs homepage (behind SSO for customers), and our site's bot protection is on. While we fix this, we also want to submit our second app, Fieldnote Forms, so both are in the queue. Also should we just set the plan to Free since we have a 14-day trial?
evals.expected_output: One fix per point: shared data bi-directional or drop write scope; remove Starter from listing pricing; public HubSpot-specific setup guide not homepage not behind SSO, allowlist HubSpot Crawler; rename app without HubSpot/Hub; do not submit second app concurrently (auto-rejected); Free only for free-forever/freemium, not trial; single resubmission.
expectations: Says to mark contacts as bi-directional in Shared data or remove the write scope if unused
Says to remove the Starter plan from listing pricing because only plans including the integration may be listed
Says the setup guide must be public, not behind login or SSO
Says the setup guide must be HubSpot-specific and not the docs homepage
Says to allowlist the HubSpot Crawler user agent in bot protection
Says the app name must not include HubSpot or Hub and proposes a renamed form
Says submitting the second app while the first is in review gets it rejected automatically
Says the Free pricing plan is only for free-forever or freemium, not a free trial
Recommends fixing all feedback points in one resubmission
Mentions writing HubSpot with a capital S across assets

evals.prompt: We've been listed on the HubSpot Marketplace for 14 months (app: Ledgerly, accounting sync). 45 active installs, 6 reviews, 3.8 average. Leadership wants us to become a Premier HubSpot technology partner and get the Certified badge next quarter. Our API success rate in the dashboard is 88%, mostly 429 errors. Marketing proposes a $25 gift card for every review to push the rating up. What's realistic?
evals.expected_output: Certification blocked until 60 active installs and success >95% (fix 429 by throttling to 100 req/10 s per account, batching, webhooks); no gift cards - review guidelines ban compensation; use 30-day review email and review link; reply to negative reviews; stars show at 10 reviews; Premier needs $7M attached MRR, 10+ reviews 4.0+, certification mandatory, exec sponsor; tier applies to account; propose realistic tier path.
expectations: States certification needs at least 60 active installs and Ledgerly has 45
States certification needs an average API success rate above 95%
Recommends throttling to HubSpot's per-account rate limit of about 100 requests per 10 seconds, or batching and webhooks, to cut 429s
Rejects the gift card plan because HubSpot's review guidelines ban compensation of any kind for reviews
Recommends HubSpot's review request email or review link sent to customers eligible under the review guidelines instead
Says the listing needs at least 10 reviews before a star rating is shown
Says replies to negative reviews are expected and checked for certification
States Premier requires attached MRR in the millions (about $7M), or the $100K influenced-deal exception that still requires every other Premier requirement
States Premier requires certification and at least 10 reviews with 4.0 or higher
States tiers are evaluated on a fixed cadence (quarterly tier-ups) over a trailing 12 months
Says certification does not by itself unlock go-to-market benefits
Recommends logging influenced deals in the developer platform to count toward tiers
